attribution.note: Zitron's own words in his own newsletter post, stated as his view.

semantics.note: The firm 'they'll be dumped en masse' is an unhedged forecast. The six-month timing and the ~9 billion shares are kept as the qualifying condition.

contract.note: Reading 'dumped en masse' as substantial, widespread selling by holders, not just eligibility or a price drop, is ordinary and fair. Using May 31, 2027 as the end of 'around six months' is reasonable.

evidence.note: Company disclosure confirming trading began Nov 19, 2026. It fixes the six-month window but says nothing about later selling.
Secondary summary of a lockup schedule that has not happened yet. It does not confirm ~9 billion eligible shares or any selling.

reviews.rationale: The forecast concerns roughly May 2027. On the evaluation date only five days of trading had passed, so the share-eligibility condition and any mass selling are still in the future. Under the policy, a forecast is not scored before its deadline.

attribution.note: Zitron's own words in his own post. The quoted tweet nearby is not part of this claim.

semantics.note: 'When it eventually falls apart, the damage will be horrendous' firmly commits to a breakdown and severe damage, with no deadline. Leaving out the remark about people celebrating does not change the core forecast.

contract.note: The plain reading, a breakdown of the NVIDIA-linked financing model causing severe harm to dependent firms, investors or lenders, is ordinary. The model's boundaries and the size of the damage are evaluator choices. Labelling the contract 'retrospective' is a minor inconsistency.

evidence.note: NVIDIA filing showing continued operations and a debt repayment. That cannot contradict an 'eventually' forecast and does not show a breakdown.

reviews.rationale: This is a firm forecast with no deadline. The packet has no documented breakdown with severe damage, and no definitive orderly wind-down of the model. NVIDIA continuing to operate does not settle an 'eventually' claim.

attribution.note: The claim rests on Zitron's own assertion. The Musk funding-gap remark is a paraphrase of someone else, used only as support, and is not scored as his claim.

semantics.note: The drafter swaps 'all this cronyism' for 'the government's intervention', which narrows and reframes the speaker's words. The contract itself notes the mismatch. The core claim, that money is running out, is a present-tense observation with a causal add-on.

contract.note: Reading 'running out' as financing resources shrinking relative to spending and obligations is a fair plain reading. The Q3 2026 window is a reasonable evaluator choice, and the contract rightly requires separate evidence for the causal 'prolong' part.

evidence.note: Crunchbase shows continued Q3 2026 venture appetite. Funding inflows alone cannot show whether liquidity was being depleted, and the item does not address the causal claim.

reviews.rationale: The packet has no industry-wide measure of liquidity against spending and obligations, and no causal evidence about the cronyism or intervention. Crunchbase inflow data weighs somewhat against a simple funding drought, but it does not settle depletion either way.

attribution.note: Zitron's own words in his own post.

semantics.note: 'The bottom will eventually fall out' is a firm forecast with no deadline. The ~80% revenue reliance on unprofitable startups is asserted as a premise and is kept as the stated reason.

contract.note: Treating the 80% premise as an antecedent that must hold for both companies is a reasonable reading, though the speaker stated it as fact rather than as an if-clause. Reading 'bottom falls out' as a severe, sustained collapse is ordinary.

evidence.note: Ramp: in its sample, 1% of businesses drive 80% of OpenAI and Anthropic revenue. That measures customer concentration, not each company's total revenue share from unprofitable AI startups. It does not establish the premise or any collapse.

reviews.rationale: The forecast has no deadline. The revenue-dependence premise is not verified for either company, and the packet shows no customer-driven collapse at either one. Nothing ends the exposure, so the claim cannot be contradicted early either.
